create.name: Albuquerque Karma Thegsum Chöling
create.bio:
Albuquerque Karma Thegsum Chöling is a small Tibetan Buddhist centre in the North Valley of Albuquerque, New Mexico, set up in 1982 as a local affiliate of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra, the monastery in Woodstock, New York, that serves as the Karmapa's North American seat. It belongs to the Karma Kagyu school, often called the practice lineage, and looks to the 17th Karmapa, Ogyen Trinley Dorje, and to the lamas of its parent monastery for guidance. The centre keeps a shrine room, a library and a small white stupa in a building set back from the road.

Every Sunday morning members chant a short liturgy of Chenrezig and Amitabha, mostly in Tibetan with an English translation, and then sit together in silent meditation; newcomers can ask for basic instruction first, and both sessions can also be joined by Zoom. Several times a year a lama from the Kagyu network comes for a weekend of talks and practice, and a Tibetan artist returns from time to time to build a sand mandala with the sangha. Membership supports the centre and its links to the parent monastery, and visitors of any background, including local college students, are welcome.

courses.title: Membership of Albuquerque KTC
courses.description: Monthly membership for individuals or families, either of the local centre alone or jointly with its parent monastery, Karma Triyana Dharmachakra. Members support the shrine room and teacher visits, borrow from the library and get reduced rates for events.
courses.price: Local KTC Member only: $15 per month

free_resources.title: Sunday sadhana and group meditation
free_resources.description: An hour of chanted Chenrezig and Amitabha practice on Sunday mornings, followed by about thirty minutes of sitting meditation with instruction on request. Open to visitors in the shrine room or online through Zoom.

free_resources.title: Chenrezig sadhana practice text
free_resources.description: The text the sangha chants at its Sunday practice, offered as a free download so that people joining in person or online can follow along.
